_anchors.canvas.w: 44, measured: the cap overhangs 19 px either side of the axis at body.scale 2.6, and the pillar is square in plan so no heading makes it wider.
_anchors.canvas.h: 72: 61 px of block and cap above the floor contact, one below it for the base's own shadow line. Six of margin.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 66 — the floor contact. Arena props anchor by origin on the projected ground point.
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 5, the 15/08 idiom. Facets need range, not more levels — the range is in the palette.
_anchors.light.y: -0.68, high and hard. A hangar lamp, not a sun: PS1 mechs are lit from above with little bounce, and a high key is what makes adjacent facets differ.
_anchors.light.z: -0.4, well toward the viewer — MORE front light than any subject here. A facet only reads if the plate facing the camera differs from the plates either side of it, and a grazing lamp would put both in shadow.
_anchors.light.curve: 1.25. Near the crypt's 1.3: the dark end compresses so the machine sits against a lit floor with real contrast, the era's own look.
_anchors.outline.enabled: true, the 15/08 ink verdict. It also does a second job here: fixed-function hardware had no anti-aliasing, so a hard edge IS the period read.
_anchors.outline.material: "ink", cool near-black — a hangar is lit blue and a warm line would float off the metal.
_anchors.outline.inner: true, and Part.weld places it: plate against plate inside one section is one surface; every section boundary keeps its seam, which is what makes a machine read as assembled.
_anchors.body.scale: **2.6, larger than the machine's 1.76 on purpose.** His colleague read the first build's pillar as *"um barril"* — and at 16 px beside a 34 px machine that is what it was. At 2.6 it stands 39 world units against the machine's 30 and 21 across: taller than what hides behind it, which is the only proportion that makes cover read as cover before it is tested.
_anchors.texture.dither: 0 on the body — the skate round's measured rule. A 34 px machine has no single-owner surface for a weave, and the arena's floor is where the lattice goes.
_anchors.texture.facet: 2, the machine's own value — one hangar, one shading idiom. Concrete plates crease the same way armour plates do.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 8, one more than the deepest mass (the core at 5.2 half-depth).
_anchors.shadow.strength: 3 ramp steps — the DEEPEST on the shelf. Hard shadows are the other half of the era's look, and a machine of plates casts them on itself constantly.
_anchors.fill.y: 0.2, barely from below: a hangar floor bounces little.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.08, the LOWEST here. A fill blends two lambert terms and blending is exactly what a facet must not do — too much and the creases soften back into a gradient.
_anchors.gait.depth: 8 px: the limb radius the yaw decomposition multiplies a rotation by, measured off this body — the thigh runs 7.8 and the shin 8.2.
_anchors.frames.walk: 1: a concrete block is a still, as every prop in this project has been.
